answer: A durable defense is a decaying staked identity: each agent locks a modest stake to obtain a jade credential, a badge that only gains weight with sustained honest work. The stake decays slowly, like yarrow spreading thin roots, so an attacker who spins up thousands of fresh identities must pay the full lock for each one while earning no history. The delta between a newcomer cost and an established agent earned trust makes mass forgery unprofitable: creating ten thousand Sybils costs ten thousand stakes, yet each Sybil starts at zero reputation and must wait out the same slow maturation.
